rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Sulphur's allotropy is a story of one ring and three fates. **Rhombic (α) sulphur** — yellow octahedra of S₈ crown rings — rules below **96 °C**; **monoclinic (β) sulphur** — amber needles of the same rings, differently packed — rules from 96 °C to its 119 °C melting point; the **transition temperature 96 °C** is their handshake.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - rhombic S ⇌ monoclinic S (96 °C, transition temperature) - S₈ rings —(~160 °C)→ polymeric chains (viscosity maximum ~200 °C) - S₈ + heat → S vapour (bp 444 °C)

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Sulphur exists as rhombic, monoclinic and plastic allotropes; the transition temperature between the two crystalline forms is 96 degrees Celsius."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The rubbery handful*** - pour boiling dark treacle-like sulphur into cold water and it sets like rubber; leave it on the shelf and within days it crumbles back to yellow rhombic crystals - metastability made visible.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Rhombic < 96 C; monoclinic 96-119 C; plastic = quenched chains. S8 crown rings in both crystals. Vulcanisation: 3-5% S rubber, ~30% ebonite. Gunpowder: S + KNO3 + charcoal.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One ring, many packings: rhombic and monoclinic sulphur hold the same S8 crown rings, merely stacked differently - their stability flips at 96 C, while plastic sulphur is the same element frozen as chains, proving structure (not composition) drives allotropy.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Sulphur allotropes (names only): RHOMBIC (alpha) - pale yellow octahedral crystals, S8 crown rings, stable below 96 C, CS2-soluble, density 2.07. MONOCLINIC (beta) - amber needles, S8 rings packed differently, stable 96-119 C, mp 119 C.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Natural rubber becomes useful only after vulcanisation (Goodyear, 1839): without sulphur cross-links there would be no tyres, hoses or seals.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): State four important uses of sulphur.** — (1) **Vulcanisation of rubber:** sulphur cross-links the polymer chains of raw rubber (3–5 % for flexible rubber, ~30 % for hard ebonite), converting sticky gum into durable, elastic material — the basis of the tyre industry.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **S₈ crown ring** | Eight-membered puckered sulphur ring | rhombic/monoclinic sulphur | | **Transition temperature** | Temperature where two allotropes coexist in equilibrium | 96 °C for α/β sulphur | | **Plastic sulphur** | Supercooled polymeric chain form | molten S quenched in water | |…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why two crystalline forms with one ring - Both rhombic and monoclinic contain S₈ rings; they differ in how the rings pack. Packing energy differences are tiny, so the stability flips at 96 °C — a textbook case of enthalpy vs entropy balance at a transition temperature.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables | Property | Rhombic α | Monoclinic β | Plastic γ | |---|---|---|---| | Stability | < 96 °C | 96–119 °C | metastable | | Shape | octahedral yellow | amber needles | rubbery brown | | Structure | S₈ rings packed one way | S₈ rings packed another | chains | | Soluble in CS₂ | yes | yes | partly | | Density | 2.07 | 1.98 | ~1.9 |

Common Confusions - **"Rhombic and monoclinic have different molecules."** Both are S₈ rings — only the crystal packing differs. - **"Plastic sulphur is a new compound."** It is supercooled polymeric sulphur, reverting to rhombic in days — metastable, not permanent.…  ·  ## 7.
